data.name: Dishant
data.gender_notes: Dishant is used as a male name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: The name Dishant is derived from the Sanskrit word ‘dhi’ which means intellect or wisdom and ‘shant’ which means calm or peace. The name signifies the will of God, the divine order, and the peaceful implementation of that will in one's life. The name Dishant carries the meaning “God's Will, Divine Order” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Dishant usually hope their child will grow to embody god's will, divine order and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.etymology: Dishant belongs to the Sanskrit linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “God's Will, Divine Order.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Dishant total 3, giving a life-path number of 3. Number 3 is linked with Jupiter and with the qualities of creativity, expression and optimism.

historical_references.reference: Dishant was a famous Jain monk and scholar from Gujarat, India, during the 4th to 5th century AD. He was a disciple of Mahavira Swetambar and contributed significantly to the Jain literature. He wrote commentaries on various Jain texts and composed several original works, including 'Tattvartha Sutra Prakashika'.

Dishant was a king reigning in the Kannada region of India around 1125 AD. He is most famous for his patronage of the Jain scholar Hemachandra, who composed the 'Kadambari', a Sanskrit epic poem. Dishant also commissioned various Jain temples and wrote Jain religious texts.
